name: Space
summary: An even, DS-scale gap between a small inline set of items — buttons, tags, inline controls.
lead: ONE custom element — <aha-space> — defined once, imported unchanged by React and Vue. Shadow-DOM CSS, themed only by --aha-* tokens; `size` takes the named steps small/middle/large (8/16/24) or a raw pixel number, `direction="vertical"` stacks the items instead, `align` sets cross-axis alignment, `wrap` lets a row flow onto multiple lines, and `split` rules a thin divider between adjacent items. Layout only — it never paints a background. Zero drift.
codeNote: Same element, same shadow-DOM CSS → identical render. React (< 19) consumes it via a thin wrapper; Vue binds the custom element natively. The primitive is defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

spec.label: Size scale
spec.value: small 8 · middle 16 · large 24 (or a raw px number)

spec.label: Wrap
spec.value: off by default; on lets a row flow onto multiple lines

props.name: size
props.desc: Gap between items — named DS step (8/16/24) or a raw pixel number

props.name: direction
props.desc: Lay items in a row or stack them

props.name: wrap
props.desc: Allow items to wrap onto multiple lines

props.name: split
props.desc: Rule a thin --aha-split divider between adjacent items

whenToUse.when: spacing a small inline set of items evenly — buttons in a toolbar, tags in a row
you need alignment/justification control over a block-level layout
the items belong in two-dimensional rows and columns

opinion.note: Space is the lightweight spacer — no alignment gymnastics, just a consistent gap. Keep sizes on the named scale so inline spacing matches across surfaces. It is layout, never decoration: it paints no background.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — DS V3 has no dedicated Space component (search_design_system on MwjvUjVI0HnfwD9EwPXRAy returns none); spec derived from the DS spacing scale (8/16/24) + AntD Space matrix (direction/size/align/wrap/split — inline gap, small default, vertical stacking, cross-axis align, row wrap, and a divider between items). A deliberate, documented layout extension; the visual tokens it binds are inherited text colour and --aha-split for the divider rule.
